title: Dropping Node 18
subtitle: Why the next release needs Node 20 or newer

scenes.narration: The next release of our command line tool stops supporting Node eighteen. Node eighteen stopped getting security fixes in April twenty twenty five, and newer Node already has what we need.
bullets: Node 18 gets [no security fixes]{bad} since April 2025
The built-in test runner is stable only from Node 20
Swapping `mocha` and `chai` for it drops **2.1 MB** of packages
About ==6% of installs== still run Node 18, so they must upgrade first
CI stops testing Node 18, which cuts each run by a third

steps.say: First, Node eighteen gets no security fixes any more.
Second, Node twenty has a stable test runner of its own, so we can drop two test packages.
The risk is the six percent of installs still on Node eighteen. They have to upgrade Node before they can update the tool.
And our own tests get a third faster, with one fewer version to run.

scenes.title: Installing on Node 18
scenes.narration: Someone still on Node eighteen gets a clear message, instead of a strange crash.

entries.output:
[error]{bad} our-cli 3.0 needs Node 20 or newer, and this is Node 18.20.4.
Upgrade Node, or keep using our-cli@2 until you can.

steps.say: Here is a machine still on Node eighteen.
Running the new version stops at once and says which Node it needs.
It also says how to keep working until they upgrade.
